sampling_model.design: Two independent samples from one population: \(\mathcal L_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\) and \(\mathcal U_m\sim P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\ge1\) labeled records and \(m\ge0\) outcome-unlabeled records with \(X\in[d]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed known constant satisfies \(0<\epsilon<1/2\); no minimum \(p_x\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Neither \(p_x\), \(e_x\), nor \(\mu_{ax}\) is known. The proved estimator uses one labeled outcome-success factor in each light-cell monomial, pooled treatment--mass factorial factors from disjoint treatment--covariate records, and an inverse-count heavy branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 gives the supervised lower scale on its stated \(d\lesssim n\log n\) regime for the same observable class modulo null-cell propensities; the all-regime supervised endpoint remains attributed to the internal matched result.
The paper gives robust and locally efficient semi-supervised ATE estimation using a small chart-reviewed sample, a larger EHR cohort, and outcome-surrogate structure.
Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.1 give an asymptotic expansion and root-\(n\) normality under explicit nuisance-error controls in a labeled--unlabeled experiment.
The paper derives regular semi-supervised efficiency and attaining estimators under support and nuisance-rate conditions rather than the present unrestricted all-regime minimax model.
The paper constructs discrete-functional estimators using factorial-moment polynomials on rare cells and a regular-cell branch, but all monomial factors arise from one observation budget.
Theorem 1 and Appendix F connect best polynomial approximation to moment-matched lower priors, without the present auxiliary-invariance and two-sample normalization requirements.

body.tldr: Gold-standard outcomes may be available for only \(n\) chart-reviewed records while treatment and baseline covariates are available for another \(m\) records. The proved minimax MSE is \(\min\{1,n^{-1}+[d/\{(n+m)\log(en)\}]^2\}\), up to constants depending only on occupied-cell overlap. A total mixed marked--unmarked polynomial estimator attains the rate, and a normalized fuzzy prior with an exactly common random \(P_{XA}\) law proves the converse. The result recovers the supervised endpoint, converges for fixed \((n,d)\) to the exact known-\(P_{XA}\) decision problem, and gives necessary and sufficient consistency, root-\(n\), and strict-improvement thresholds.

project_justification.gap: Existing discrete-ATE theory resolves the labeled-only rare-cell barrier, while semi-supervised causal analyses give regular local efficiency under nuisance consistency or working models. Neither line supplies the finite-sample minimax experiment in which outcome-bearing moments have size \(n\) and treatment--mass moments have size \(n+m\), with null cells and unrestricted outcome regressions.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an all-regime annotation frontier whose estimator uses at most one labeled outcome factor in each polynomial monomial and whose lower prior is invisible to the entire auxiliary sample, not merely moment-matched after marginal perturbations.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the frontier \(R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\asymp_\epsilon\min\{1,n^{-1}+[d/\{(n+m)\log(en)\}]^2\}\). The upper proof controls false-light polynomial tails and random branch means by mass weighting, and the lower proof combines reciprocal-approximation duality, label-gated likelihood cancellation, reservoir normalization, and fixed-sample transfer. It also proves an inverse-count fallback \(R_\epsilon\lesssim_\epsilon\min\{1,n^{-1}+[d/(n+m)]^2\}\), the uniform \(d=2\) rate, the fixed-parameter oracle-risk limit, and exact sequence thresholds.

body.related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024}, establish the supervised discrete-covariate obstruction on the same observable class modulo immaterial null-cell propensities; their Theorem 2 is scoped to the stated labeled-only regime, so the uniform \(m=0\) endpoint here remains attributed to the catalogued \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap}\) result. Cheng, Ananthakrishnan, and Cai, \cite{ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021}, Sections 2.1 and 4, provide the chart-review motivation and a robust locally efficient procedure using outcome surrogates. Chakrabortty and Dai, \cite{ChakraborttyDai2024}, and Kato, \cite{Kato2025}, give adjacent two-cohort efficiency and nuisance-rate results. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015}, motivate the heavy--light polynomial architecture, while Wu and Yang, \cite{WuYang2016}, Appendix F, provide the approximation--moment duality used by the converse. The new step is the unequal-information coupling: outcome-marked factors use only labeled records, higher marginal factorial factors use pooled records, and the lower hypotheses preserve the full random \(P_{XA}\) law.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The constants produced by the Chebyshev coefficient envelope, pilot Chernoff bounds, and Poisson-prefix transfer are conservative and are not optimized. The exact convergence to the known-\(P_{XA}\) minimax risk is proved only for fixed \(n,d\), not for triangular arrays. The theorem concerns MSE point estimation in the unrestricted finite-alphabet model; it does not construct confidence intervals, exploit post-treatment outcome surrogates, or address nonrandom validation.
body.honest_scope: Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and occupied-cell overlap, the causal ATE equals the observed-law functional \(\tau(P)=\sum_xp_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x})\). The theorem is uniform over arbitrary cell masses, including null cells, and assumes neither smoothness, sparsity, effect homogeneity, outcome surrogacy, nor a minimum cell mass. The auxiliary sample is iid from the same \(P_{XA}\) and independent of the labeled sample. The result is a baseline-only discrete benchmark for choosing additional chart labels versus additional treatment--covariate records in the Cheng--Ananthakrishnan--Cai setting; it neither claims their surrogate-based efficiency nor validates their empirical data under this unrestricted model.
body.interpretation: Let \(N=n+m\). Consistency requires and is guaranteed by \(d=o\{N\log(en)\}\); root-\(n\) MSE requires and is guaranteed by \(d=O\{N\log(en)/\sqrt n\}\). Thus auxiliary treatment--covariate records can remove the high-cardinality approximation term but cannot improve the irreducible \(n^{-1}\) outcome-label floor. Strict order improvement over supervised estimation occurs exactly when the supervised rare-cell term dominates \(n^{-1}\) and the auxiliary enlargement is large enough relative to that term, as stated in the frontier theorem.
